title: Bose Brought Back Wired Headphones, and Teens Are to Thank
gist: Wired headphone sales are growing for the first time in five years (+10% in 2H 2025, +20% in early 2026), led by Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Bose is responding with $99 Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds, its first wired headphones in 11 years, built from idea to product in about 8-9 months. The article reads as an early hands-on of a late-stage prototype.

insights.claim: Wired headphone sales rose for the first time in five years, up 10 percent in the second half of 2025 and 20 percent at the start of 2026.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Growth is speeding up in a category many had written off, which could lift sales for audio makers and accessory retailers.
insights.quote: sales up for the first time in five years—10 percent in the back half of 2025 and 20 percent at the start of 2026

insights.claim: Young consumers (Gen Z and Gen Alpha) are driving the wired-earbud revival, helped by celebrities who wear wired earbuds and even write songs about them.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Demand driven by culture and fashion can grow fast, but it can also fade fast, so it is a riskier base for long product plans.
insights.quote: Young people are driving the trend, including celebrities sporting wired earbuds and literally writing songs about them.

insights.claim: Bose's president of consumer audio, Raza Haider, spotted the trend first-hand when he dropped his teen off at college and saw wired earbuds everywhere.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: An incumbent is making product calls from what its leaders see around them, not only from sell-through data.
insights.quote: He dropped off his teen at college last year and saw wired earbuds left and right.

insights.claim: Part of the appeal of wired headphones is what they leave out: no battery to charge, no app, no Bluetooth pairing, and no latency for TV or games.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: This is a pushback against wireless and app-heavy devices, and it could hold down premium TWS pricing at the entry level.
insights.quote: There’s no battery to charge, no app to download, no Bluetooth to fiddle with, and no latency to ruin your TV show or video game.

insights.claim: The author notes that wired earbuds never actually went away, and names alternatives such as the Sennheiser IE200 ($160, discounted to $130) and the $20 Final E500.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Bose is entering a crowded field where prices run from $20 to $160, so its brand alone may not guarantee a premium.
insights.quote: wired earbuds never truly went away

insights.claim: Bose is launching $99 Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds, its first wired headphones in about 11 years, timed to capture the wired revival.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: A major audio brand moving back into wired products supports the idea that the trend will last beyond a niche.
insights.quote: The new $99 Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds come to the market just in time to capitalize on this trend.

insights.claim: Bose took the earbuds from idea to final product in about eight or nine months, which the reviewer calls much faster than typical audio launches. This follows a company-wide effort to speed up production, revisions, and collaborations.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Faster product cycles let a hardware incumbent chase short-lived consumer trends before they peak.
insights.quote: Bose has been working toward enabling faster, more efficient production to accelerate new product launches, revisions, and collaborations.

insights.claim: In early testing of a late-stage prototype, the Bose earbuds beat cheaper wired options such as Apple EarPods on both sound quality and active noise cancelling.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Built-in ANC sets the product apart in a low-cost category and supports a $99 price.
insights.quote: the Bose earbuds leapfrog cheaper wired pairs (like Apple EarPods) in sound quality and active noise canceling (ANC)

insights.claim: The main design weakness is a heavy inline control panel that pulls on the cable and the earbuds, adding tension that wireless earbuds avoid.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Adding ANC to a wired design costs some comfort, which could limit how widely the product is adopted.
insights.quote: The cable tension it adds is annoying, especially compared to the tension-free experience of using wireless earbuds.

insights.claim: The earbuds ship October 15 in black, white, and a limited-edition mint, with preorders at Bose and Best Buy.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Q4 holiday timing and Best Buy distribution put the product in the peak buying season.
